article.heading: Why split a PDF locally instead of uploading it?
article.p1: A scanned book, a bundle of monthly statements, a 200-page report you only need three pages from — sooner or later a PDF grows too large or too mixed-purpose for what you actually need. Most free "split PDF" websites handle this the same way the free "merge PDF" sites do: by quietly uploading your file to a server before doing anything with it. That's a strange amount of trust to hand over for a document that might contain a signature, a bank statement, or a page you'd rather not have sitting on someone else's disk.
article.p2: This tool never uploads anything. It runs entirely in your browser using pdf-lib, a JavaScript library that reads the raw structure of your PDF and copies only the pages you asked for into brand-new documents, assembled in memory on your own device. Page thumbnails are rendered locally too, with pdf.js — the same engine built into Firefox — so you can see exactly what's on each page before deciding how to split it.
article.p3: Select a PDF file or drag it into the drop zone; every page appears as its own thumbnail so you can see the document at a glance. Rotate a page 90° at a time or delete one entirely if it shouldn't be in any of the output files — a blank scanned sheet, for instance. Then choose how to split: Custom ranges lets you type groups like "1-3, 4, 5-7" where each comma-separated group becomes its own file, while Every N pages automatically chops the document into equal-sized chunks — useful for breaking a long scan into, say, 10-page pieces without typing out every range by hand. Press Split PDF and each result appears with its own download button.
article.p4: There's no page limit built into the tool, though very large scanned PDFs full of images will naturally take a little longer to render thumbnails for since everything runs on your own device rather than a server farm. If you type a range that doesn't make sense — a page number beyond the document's length, or text that isn't a valid range — the tool tells you exactly which part was invalid instead of producing a broken file. If you later need to put pages from several PDFs back together, the Merge PDF tool works the same privacy-first way and shares the same rotate-and-delete page controls.
